AC: Answers: does cosine-vs-candidates zero-shot tagging work on this corpus? Verdict + numbered evidence with numbers, symptoms, conclusions, and a prioritized next-step list whose first item is the single cheapest decisive experiment. Falsifiable: gold labels and method stated so any claim can be rechecked.

Body.raw:
VERDICT (2026-08-05): zero-shot tagging by cosine-vs-candidates DOES NOT WORK on
this corpus, and the defect is the EMBEDDING SPACE, not the candidate domain.
0 of 36 mined-domain cells produced a usable topical tag. A curated,
uniform-length label set -- the cleanest domain possible -- scored
precision@1 = 0/6. Do not spend more effort on candidate-domain variations.

Predecessor: ef4ad78d (shipped the machinery; its own follow-up list is largely
invalidated by this spike). Successor: 91e28fd0 (tuned importance pipeline).

=== EXPERIMENT DESIGN (reproducible from this description) ===

Embedder: apple (Apple NLContextualEmbedding via the Swift sidecar), 512-dim,
mean-pooled, l2-normalized. The only production embedder; `hash` was removed
2026-08-04.

Subjects: 6 todos chosen for maximum topic separation and mixed body length.
  515fc9ea  test sqlite storage suite            87 chars    1 chunk
  cc756c32  wt-inventory old worktrees          123 chars    1 chunk
  a31d8f24  vec search ranking                   95 chars    1 chunk
  a46c04b0  flac directory names from metadata  666 chars   15 chunks
  21e3454c  ESP32 /healthz and /logs endpoints  941 chars   51 chunks
  ef4ad78d  zero-shot semantic tagging        7,317 chars  420 chunks

Gold labels (stated up front so results are falsifiable):
  515fc9ea -> automated testing / sqlite storage
  cc756c32 -> git worktrees
  a31d8f24 -> vector search ranking
  a46c04b0 -> audio (flac) file/directory naming from metadata
  21e3454c -> esp32 embedded http endpoints
  ef4ad78d -> semantic tagging with embeddings

Candidate domains:
  A  subject n-phrases    483 -- 1..3-phrase windows from the 6 subjects only
  B  corpus n-phrases   4,639 -- 1..3-phrase windows from all 55 todos (shipped)
  C  corpus keywords    2,697 -- word-level 1..3-grams, all 55 todos, freq >= 2
                                 (26,280 raw uniques; hapax-filtered)
  D  curated labels         14 -- 2-3 word concept labels, 10 real + 4 distractors

Document granularity:
  whole -- one vector for Summary+Body concatenated (what the shipped tagger does)
  chunk -- one vector per 1..3-phrase window, candidate scored by MAX over chunks

Corrections tried: none (raw cosine), and per-candidate z-score across all 55
docs (the hubness correction ef4ad78d specified and never implemented).

Metrics: precision@1/@3 vs gold; score spread; count of candidates within 0.01
of rank-1; whether rank-1 was sourced from the subject itself.

=== EVIDENCE ===

1. COSINE RANKS CANDIDATE LENGTH, NOT TOPIC.
   Fixed target (flac/audio metadata), irrelevant candidate grown word by word:
     1 word  'git'                                            +0.476
     4 words 'git branch checkout worktree'                   +0.832
     7 words '... inventory teardown stale'                   +0.875
     13 words '... commit push merge rebase origin master'    +0.895
   Relevant candidates for the same target:
     1 word  'flac'                                           +0.645
     2 words 'audio metadata'                                 +0.698
     5 words 'flac audio metadata directory naming'           +0.916
   A 13-word IRRELEVANT candidate (0.895) beats the 2-word RELEVANT
   'audio metadata' (0.698) by +0.20. Topic wins only when it is also long.

2. THE NUISANCE IS ~10x THE SIGNAL.
   Mean cosine of each curated label to all 55 corpus docs, with its sd:
     +0.8138  sd=0.0174  billing and invoicing      <-- DISTRACTOR, top hub
     +0.7776  sd=0.0260  command line interface
     +0.7685  sd=0.0207  embedded hardware
     +0.7428  sd=0.0211  git worktrees
     +0.7280  sd=0.0178  semantic tagging
     +0.7150  sd=0.0251  audio file metadata
     +0.7140  sd=0.0310  sqlite storage
     +0.7120  sd=0.0266  automated testing
     +0.7090  sd=0.0301  vector search
     +0.6942  sd=0.0256  user interface design      <-- distractor
     +0.6924  sd=0.0240  schema migration
     +0.6913  sd=0.0304  network routing            <-- distractor
     +0.6688  sd=0.0331  firmware updates
     +0.6173  sd=0.0331  access control             <-- distractor
   Between-label spread = 0.20. Within-label variation across documents =
   sd ~0.02. The label's fixed position dominates by an order of magnitude:
   WHICH DOCUMENT YOU SCORE BARELY MOVES THE NUMBER. And the strongest hub is a
   distractor -- 'billing and invoicing' is closer to all 55 todos than every
   relevant label, with the lowest variance, and takes rank 1 for 5 of 6
   subjects.

3. BARE NUMERALS ARE DEGENERATE HUBS.
   cos('5','6') = 0.9932   cos('6','7') = 0.9941   cos('5','8') = 0.9881
   cos('5','five') = 0.5427  cos('5','testing') = 0.5564
   Not number semantics -- short digit strings collapse to one point. Numbered
   lists in bodies yield bare-digit phrase windows, so chunk-max matches
   digit-to-digit and beats every real phrase. On ef4ad78d/chunk: rank-1 =
   1.0000 with 318 of 483 candidates within 0.01 of it, median 0.9938. The
   entire domain is effectively one point.

4. SELF-MATCH IS UNAVOIDABLE IN MINED DOMAINS.
   Rank 1 was the subject's OWN sentence in 12/12 of the A and B cells
   (0.985-1.000). At chunk granularity it is exactly 1.0000 -- the todo matching
   its own phrase verbatim. Any mined domain must exclude self-sourced
   candidates or the output is tautological.

5. DOMAIN SCOPE MADE NO DIFFERENCE.
   A (483, subjects only) vs B (4,639, whole corpus): same rank-1s, same ~0.98
   scores, medians within 0.005. Shrinking the domain 10x changed nothing.

6. SCORE COMPRESSION.
   Domains A/B: median cosine 0.87-0.93, rank-1 ~0.98 -- thousands of candidates
   inside a 0.10 band. Curated domain D: total spread across 14 wildly different
   labels was only 0.06-0.26. No threshold can separate a good tag from a bad one.

7. PER-CANDIDATE Z-SCORE HELPS, THEN FAILS DIFFERENTLY.
   It correctly cancels the per-candidate length offset and produced the FIRST
   correct answers in the whole spike:
     515fc9ea -> 'test coverage of the tag feature'      (+1.74 sigma)
     cc756c32 -> 'that branch and its worktree'          (+3.42 sigma)
   But on keyword domain C it inverts into a RARITY bias, promoting dates
   ('2026-07-20'), identifiers ('ce147239', 'sha256'), ASCII table borders, and
   near-stopwords ('rather', 'partly', 'questions'). ~2/6 at best. Necessary,
   nowhere near sufficient: after removing the offset only sd~0.02 of real signal
   remains, and other artifacts dominate it.

8. GRANULARITY ONLY RESCUES VERY LONG DOCUMENTS.
   Chunking produced the single genuine hit of the curated arm -- ef4ad78d
   (420 chunks): 'vector search' +0.9071 and 'semantic tagging' +0.8939 as ranks
   1 and 2, both correct. It HURT the mid-size doc 21e3454c (51 chunks):
   whole = hit@3 -> chunk = MISS, spread collapsing 0.189 -> 0.084. More chunks
   means more chances for a hub to max out.

=== SYMPTOMS (how this presents in production) ===

- Tags are long sentence fragments lifted from unrelated todos.
- Tags include bare digits, dates, file paths, ASCII art.
- A few candidates recur across topically unrelated todos.
- Every score is ~0.9, so no threshold separates good from bad.
- Todos tagged with their own text.

All of these matched the real store before it was cleared: ef4ad78d's three
automatic tags were long fragments mined from an unrelated todo about
"relationship kinds".

=== CONCLUSIONS ===

1. As shipped the method does not work -- 0/36, not marginal.
2. The candidate domain is NOT the problem. Subject-scoped, corpus-scoped, and
   word-level keyword domains all fail. This invalidates ef4ad78d follow-up #3
   (mine word n-grams) and the "shrink the domain" idea as fixes.
3. Granularity is NOT the problem, except as a rescue for very long documents.
4. The z-score (ef4ad78d follow-up #2) is necessary but NOT sufficient.
5. Curating the vocabulary does NOT save it. This is the decisive result: with
   the domain perfect by construction, a distractor still beats the truth 5/6
   times. That isolates the embedder as the defect.
6. Apple NLCE is unfit for zero-shot topical assignment on this corpus. This
   confirms 91e28fd0's own note ("compressed cosine range, keys on shared
   surface tokens over concept") with a gold standard and numbers.
7. Removing `hash` was correct, but switching auto-tagging to `apple` would NOT
   have worked either. Auto-tagging staying dormant is the right state.

=== NEXT STEPS (in priority order) ===

1. CHEAPEST DECISIVE TEST: re-run the curated 6-subject arm (domain D, whole +
   chunk, raw cosine, precision@1/@3) against the `st` backend --
   sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2, already registered hidden in
   todo_embed._BACKENDS, selectable as --embedder st. One flag, ~2 minutes.
   MiniLM is TRAINED for sentence-level semantic similarity rather than
   token-level contextual embedding, so it is the single variable most likely to
   move precision@1 off zero.
   - If it works: auto-tagging becomes viable on a curated label set + st, and
     the hubness z-score should be added on top.
   - If it also fails: the conclusion generalizes from "wrong embedder" to
     "wrong architecture", and 91e28fd0's tuned-scorer pipeline is the only
     remaining path. Record that either way -- it is the key branch point.
2. Whatever embedder is chosen, apply BOTH corrections before top-k:
   per-candidate z-score across the corpus (kills the length/hub offset) AND a
   candidate filter dropping bare numerals, 1-char tokens, dates, hex
   identifiers and ASCII-art runs (proven artifacts, item 3/7 above).
3. Prefer a CURATED label set over mined candidates. Mined domains additionally
   require self-source exclusion (item 4) and still emit sentence fragments.
4. Re-arming is automatic: `_recompute_auto_tags` stands down only because
   `todo_embed.cheap_embedders()` is empty. Registering a cheap semantic backend
   turns it back on -- so DO NOT register one until precision@1 is acceptable on
   a gold set, or the corpus refills with noise.
5. Guard the zero-vector failure mode first: `_is_vector` accepts an all-zero
   vector as present and `cosine_similarity` returns 0.0 for a zero-norm input
   instead of raising, so the trust-existing backfill never repairs one. 77% of
   stored apple vectors were inert this way before 0b6b738 repaired them.

=== NOTES ===

Experiment scripts were session scratch and are NOT preserved; the design
section above is sufficient to rebuild them. Nothing in this spike wrote to the
store. Method summary: embed candidates once, cache, score each subject by
cosine (whole-field vector, or max over per-n-phrase-window vectors), sort
descending with ties broken on candidate text ascending, take top-k.

Summary.raw: spike to find next steps in oneshot tagging and embedding
